race_context: The 'Clinton Prairie School Board' seats belong to Clinton Prairie School Corporation, west of Frankfort in Clinton County, formed in 1962 by consolidating the schools of Washington, Jackson, Madison and Perry townships; it runs Clinton Prairie Elementary and Clinton Prairie Jr./Sr. High School on one campus {cp_welcome}. Federal data list 1,153 students in 2024-25 {nces_cp}. John C. Sampson became superintendent under a contract running July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029 {cp_supt_contract}.

The board has five members: four township representatives (Jackson, Washington, Madison and Perry) and one at-large member {cp_board}. Current members are Justin Brewer (president, at large), Bobbi Elliott (vice president, Jackson Township), David Larsh (secretary, Perry Township), Kerk Kesler (Washington Township) and Adam Beck (Madison Township) {cp_board}. This guide did not find the district's written election plan, so it could not confirm whether every voter in the corporation votes for every seat.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: two seats, each electing one member, consistent with the state list's 'vote for 1' {in_list}{ft_2022_results}. In 2022, Justin Brewer won the At Large seat over Rob Allen (51.34% to 48.66%), and Cynthia Neal won District 17 over Toby Boyer (63.90% to 36.10%) {ft_2022_results}. Neal is no longer listed as a board member; the board now lists Kerk Kesler as the Washington Township representative, which appears to be the District 17 seat {cp_board}{in_list}.

Who is running: Kerk Kesler, now on the board, faces Rob Allen in District 17, and board president Justin Brewer faces Michael Aaron Boesch for the At Large seat; all four are listed as Republicans {in_list}{cp_board}. A 2025 state law (Senate Enrolled Act 287) let school board candidates list a party for the first time in 2026 {ft_party_split}.

Superintendent change (2026): the signed contract with John C. Sampson runs July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029 {cp_supt_contract}. An Aug. 17, 2026 hearing covered amendments that drop the board's 3% payment to the state teachers' retirement fund on the superintendent's behalf and raise its 401(a) contribution from 3% to 6% of base salary {cp_supt_amend}.

Teacher pay (2026-27): a tentative agreement dated Sept. 29, 2026 with the Clinton Prairie Classroom Teachers' Association adds $650 to every teacher's base salary, a $350 stipend for every teacher, and an extra stipend of $241 to $1,085 if the February 2027 enrollment count is at least two students higher than October 2026 {cp_cba_2026}. The board scheduled a public hearing on the agreement for Oct. 8, 2026, after a Sept. 1 hearing set to take public testimony before bargaining began {cp_cba_2026}{ccdn_cp_0901}.

Budget and capital plans: the board scheduled a hearing on its 2027 capital projects plan for Sept. 21, 2026 {cp_cap_plan} and a public hearing on its proposed 2027 budget for Oct. 8, 2026 {ccdn_cp_budget}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects the district and no operating or safety referendum.

Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the candidates' views. The board meets at 6 p.m. on the third Monday of each month; agendas and minutes are posted on BoardDocs and meetings are streamed on YouTube {cp_agendas}.
